title: control-plane/db: add migration metadata table for downgrade guardrails + forward-only detection
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: - Control plane DB now records per-migration metadata (checksum, applied_by_version, forward_only flag) to enable safer downgrade/rollback checks in Private upgrade workflows.
description:
Context: Private upgrade/rollback needs a deterministic way to answer “is rollback safe?” after an upgrade attempt, especially when DB migrations are involved. Historically we only tracked applied migration IDs (via schema_migrations) which is insufficient to detect (a) forward-only migrations and (b) migrations that are theoretically reversible but were applied by a control plane version that we won’t support downgrading past.

This PR introduces a migration metadata table and updates the migration runner to populate it for every applied migration. The metadata enables downgrade guardrails in the control plane and in the private installer/helm hooks (follow-up PRs) without requiring parsing migration source or relying on deployment-time assumptions.

What’s in this PR: (1) New table: schema_migrations_metadata (Postgres) keyed by migration_id with checksum, applied_at, applied_by_version, forward_only, and notes (freeform) + indexes for lookup. (2) Migration runner changes: when applying a migration, compute a stable checksum of the migration content (for SQL) or declared checksum (for code-based migrations), read optional attributes from the migration header (forward_only: true/false), and write/UPSERT metadata in the same transaction as schema_migrations update. (3) API surface (internal): add a small internal helper to query “latest forward-only migration applied” and “is downgrade to version X allowed” based on applied_by_version + forward_only. (4) Backfill behavior: existing installs will have metadata rows backfilled lazily on first migration run (best-effort); for installs where historical migration content isn’t available, checksum will be recorded as ‘unknown’ and forward_only defaults to false (safe default is handled by guardrails: unknown => treat as forward-only for rollback checks; see notes below). (5) Tests: unit tests for checksum stability, metadata upsert semantics, and rollback safety query logic; integration test spins up postgres, applies migrations twice, validates idempotency and query results.

Design notes / guardrails: - forward_only semantics: forward_only means we will not run “down” for this migration and rollback must stop before this boundary. - Unknown metadata: if checksum/attributes can’t be resolved for an old migration, we record unknown and mark forward_only_unknown = true internally; downgrade checks treat this as “not rollback safe” unless explicitly overridden by operator tooling. (Operator override is NOT added here; that lives in installer UX.) - applied_by_version: derived from REDWOOD_BUILD_VERSION (control plane) at migration time. Downgrade checks compare target version < max(applied_by_version) and will return “requires snapshot restore” when version skew is detected.

Why now: This is a prerequisite for the Private upgrade plan and rollback hooks work (ENG-2318). It also addresses ambiguity called out in SUP-1842 where a customer asked whether rollback was safe after a partial upgrade that included a schema migration.

How to test: - Local: run control plane with a fresh postgres; apply migrations; confirm schema_migrations_metadata has rows and is updated on re-run. - Safety queries: call internal helper IsDowngradeAllowed(targetVersion) and verify it blocks when a forward_only migration exists or metadata is unknown. - Existing DB: run migrations on a DB that already has schema_migrations; verify lazy backfill populates rows and does not error.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire downgrade guardrails into the private installer’s “upgrade plan” and “rollback” commands (installer will query control plane endpoint /versions + migration safety status). - Helm migration job annotations to mark forward-only boundaries for operator visibility. - Document the operator policy around “unknown metadata” and snapshot-based rollback.

conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee the metadata write is in the same tx as schema_migrations update? If not, we can end up with applied migrations without metadata and that’s exactly what the installer will be relying on.

Michael Nguyen (author): Yep — runner wraps apply + schema_migrations insert + metadata upsert in a single transaction. Added a test that forces an error after metadata write to confirm rollback rolls both back.

Connor O'Brien (review): For Private rollback, “unknown => block rollback” is the safer stance. Right now description says defaults to false but guardrails treat unknown as not safe. Can we make that explicit in code naming? The installer UX will depend on this distinction.

Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. Renamed internal field to metadataUnknown and made downgrade check treat metadataUnknown as forward-only boundary. Updated comments + added a unit test for unknown handling.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please add an index for lookup by applied_at desc (we’ll query most recent forward-only/unknown during incidents). Also, ensure we don’t log raw migration content when computing checksum.
Michael Nguyen (author): Added index (applied_at desc) and confirmed we only hash bytes in-memory; no logs. Added a brief note in code comments and ensured debug logging prints migration_id only.

Marcus Lin (security review): Is applied_by_version user-controlled? We should treat it as untrusted input (env var) and avoid using it for anything security-sensitive. Also: any PII risk? Probably none, but please confirm notes field is not exposed externally.

Michael Nguyen (author): applied_by_version comes from build metadata but agreed it’s not a trust boundary. This is only used for operational guardrails. notes is not surfaced on external APIs; only internal DB. Added a comment and ensured it’s excluded from any future endpoint shape (will be separate PR).
Benji Okafor (review): For code-based migrations, how do we get a stable checksum? If it’s based on compiled output it’ll change. Prefer explicit checksum constant or file hash at build time.

Michael Nguyen (author): Implemented explicit checksum declaration for code migrations (Checksum() string) with fallback to ‘unknown’ if not provided. Added tests to ensure we don’t compute from compiled bytes.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM after index + naming cleanup. This unblocks the rollback safety endpoint work.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved. Please link the follow-up installer/endpoint PRs when they’re up.
Merge bot: Squash and merged into main.
